plan: This is a single-round auction, so there's no learning to be done from previous rounds. My value is $30. I need to consider how Betty and Charles might bid. A simple strategy is to bid slightly below my value, say $29.9. If they bid lower than that, I win and make a profit. If they bid higher, I lose, which is better than winning and losing money. Let's assume they bid their values. I will bid $29.9.

I will start with a baseline strategy of bidding my value minus a small amount to try and secure a profit. I'll bid $33. This allows me to win if the other bidders have lower values, and still make a profit. If I bid higher, I risk paying more than my value. If I bid lower, I risk losing out on a potential win. Given this is the first round, I have no prior information about the other bidders' strategies.

My value is $6. I expect the other bidders, Andy and Betty, to bid somewhat lower than their values, but not necessarily optimally. A simple strategy is to bid slightly below my value, say $5.9. If they bid their values, I win when both their values are lower than mine. If they bid lower than their values, I have a higher chance of winning, but might overpay if their second highest bid is close to my value. I will bid $5.9.
